findings.title: Fallback bundles are not loaded on the translation path
findings.body: I18n::Backend::Fallbacks resolves SiteSetting.default_locale and :en inside the backend, but the on-demand loader only runs for the active locale. I18n.translate (line 68) calls load_locale(config.locale) and never consults I18n.fallbacks, and backend fallback lookups do not go back through I18n.translate, so those YAML files stay unloaded. The new ensure_loaded! helper is only called from ApplicationController#set_locale. Mailers, jobs, rake tasks, console use, and I18n.with_locale / I18n.t(locale:) that never hit that filter therefore miss fallback strings and return a missing-translation result even when the site locale or English has the key. Argument-less lookups then store that failure in the process-wide LRU (line 74). Hot keys are not evicted, so one early lookup permanently poisons later requests in the same process even after ensure_loaded! has loaded the files.

findings.title: Translation cache key ignores dynamic fallback locale
findings.body: FallbackLocaleList#[] re-reads SiteSetting.default_locale on every lookup so the fallback language can change without a restart, but the accelerator cache key is only "#{key}#{config.locale}#{backend.object_id}". Nothing clears @cache when the site locale changes. Argument-less I18n.t results — including strings taken from the previous default locale and cached missing-translation placeholders — remain in the 300-entry LRU, and frequently used keys are never evicted. After an admin changes default_locale, users whose own locale lacks those keys keep seeing the old fallback language until the process is restarted. Interpolated calls skip the cache, so the same copy can also disagree with itself depending on whether it has interpolations.

findings.title: No tests for fallback order, loading, or cache interaction
findings.body: The new user-locale → SiteSetting.default_locale → :en chain, ensure_loaded!, and the accelerator cache have no coverage. Fallbacks are now installed in every environment (previously only production/profile), so tests that expected a missing non-English key to raise or return a missing-translation string will silently get English instead, and the job/mailer load gap and stale-cache-after-default-locale-change bugs above would not be caught. A controller example and a non-request I18n.t (after setting a non-English locale whose fallback files are not yet loaded) need to assert both the fallback order and that a miss is not cached before the fallback bundles are loaded.
